# Vendored crates

## Window-stack provenance after the egui 0.37 migration

The checked-in, resolved Cargo graph pins `winit` to storytold/winit
`a517b3846ee8457d84ee4975110bfda6797c44dc` and the egui crates to storytold/egui
`6d518fc799681571963842f95b55a6b68431b15a`. Neither `vendor/winit` nor
`vendor/egui-wgpu` is a root `[patch.crates-io]` path entry. The retained copies
record the app's earlier patches; their source-reading tests establish provenance,
while the resolved forks and their behavioral tests establish runtime behavior.

The retained winit copy has upstream base `e9809ef54b18499bb4f2cac945719ecc2a61061b`,
as recorded in `vendor/winit/.cargo_vcs_info.json`. Its thirteen patch rows below
match the fork's `PATCHES.md` entries W1–W13 commit for commit (W1 `b357a332`,
W2 `13ca693b`, W3 `fd104a4c`, W4 `3fffb7ce`, W5 `283370ce`, W6 `a82b90fb`,
W7 `9b90d5bd`, W8 `6a87addd`, W9 `9500f25d`, W10 `4a7dd791`, W11 `4df8554b`,
W12 `7facf001`, W13 `5506b1a9`). The reviewed winit fork additionally carries
W14–W27 (W14 is opt-in and is not enabled by PdfCraft). `vendor/egui-wgpu` carries
E2 (`surface_fit`) and E3 (`catch_errors`); the egui-wgpu 0.37 fork retains both,
including its `surface_fit` tests exercised by PdfCraft's behavioral tests.

Keep both copies while their provenance tests remain in use. Renderer and security
vendors below retain their independent path patches and licenses.

Permissively licensed crates we carry small patches for. Each directory keeps the upstream
licence files unchanged. Every patch is marked `PdfCraft patch:` in the source, is covered by a
PdfCraft test, and should be proposed upstream. Remove the vendored copy once upstream releases
the fix. Vendoring copyleft code is never allowed (plan/adr/0001).

A PdfCraft patch in `hayro-syntax::Page::base_dimensions` expresses the existing one-point floor as a raw reciprocal of `/UserUnit`, rounded upward only when f32 multiplication would fall below one point. Five `pdfcraft-render` regressions with prefix `raster::tests::raw_crop_` cover the observed dimensions, origins and rotations, units 41/47, bounded vector rasters and unchanged nearly-zero A4 fallback. Accepted page-unit policy and licences are unchanged.

In `hayro-interpret`, Type 3 glyph bounding boxes are transformed to device space before intersecting clip and shading bounds; `raster::tests::shaded_type3_glyph_draws_at_multiple_positions` covers translated glyphs (#3178).

Named form properties use the effective page dictionary when the form omits `/Resources` (#3574).
`hayro-syntax::Resources` caches the page origin; `hayro-interpret` preserves the form dictionary's absence.
An own dictionary stops fallback, including empty and malformed entries. Explicit null keeps its previous local-empty behavior.
`crates/render/tests/named_form_properties.rs` covers text, Find, OCG identity, visibility overrides, page inheritance, and save/reopen.
Other resource categories retain their existing parent-chain lookup.

| hayro-interpret | 0.7.0 | Apache-2.0 OR MIT | (1) select `/AP /N` appearance states via `/AS` (checkboxes, radios, stateful icons) and honour the NoView flag; (2) Type3 Unicode fallback to `/Encoding` glyph names, then printable ASCII; (3) `Type3Glyph::advance_width`; (4) `InterpreterSettings::ocg_overrides` for viewer layer toggles; (5) soft masks whose group lacks `/CS` were dropped (Chrome gradient text); (6) paint nesting cap `MAX_PAINT_NESTING` for tiling patterns and Type 3 glyphs (self-referencing content overflowed the stack); (7) CID width ranges in `/W` and `/W2` clamped to `MAX_CID` (a `0 4294967295 w` range hung); (8) `InterpreterSettings::hide_comments` skips markup annotations but keeps widgets and links (View ▸ Hide all comments); (11) depends on skrifa 0.47 instead of 0.42 (upstream read-fonts fixed a Type 1 tokenizer that recursed through runs of numbers: a fuzzed font hung or overflowed the stack), with the one API change (`Charset::glyph_id` returns `Option`); (12) annotation appearances whose `/BBox` or `/Matrix` collapses to a line or a point are skipped (mapping them onto `/Rect` divided by zero and handed the device infinite or NaN matrices); (13) a Highlight annotation without a usable normal appearance is drawn from its `/QuadPoints`, `/C` and `/CA` with Multiply blending, as pdfcraft-annot draws highlights (it was not drawn at all); (14) simple-font `/Widths` (`read_widths`): entries only for codes 0–255 (one entry per code below `/FirstChar` was allocated: `4294967295` asked for 34 GB), an entry that isn't a number leaves its code missing instead of ending the array, and a `/LastChar` below `/FirstChar` gives no widths instead of discarding the font for a standard one; (15) the appearance box is mapped onto `/Rect` corner to corner: the translation now accounts for the scale (an appearance whose box didn't start at the origin and differed in size from `/Rect` was drawn shifted); (16) a clip set by `W`/`W*` takes effect after whichever path-painting operator ends the path (`S`, `f`, `B`, … as well as `n`; ISO 32000-2 §8.5.4): it was applied only on `n`, so `re W* S` clipped nothing and the clip stayed pending for a later, unrelated `n`; (17) `InterpreterSettings::cancelled`: once set, interpretation stops before the next content operator (a render pool sets it for every worker when dropped, after an edit or on closing, and for one worker when the watchdog gives up on its render, so renders whose answers nobody can receive stop instead of running to the end); (18) `MAX_PAGE_CONTENT`: the content a page holds at once (its contents, and the forms, tiling patterns and Type 3 glyph procedures being painted) stays within 512 MiB (`decode_content`; once it runs out, `InterpreterWarning::ContentTruncated` is reported (once per page by pdfcraft-render) so a truncated page is not a clean render; each level gives its bytes back when it finishes): forms nest fifty deep and each level kept its content while the next ran, so a form painting itself around a stream inflating to 256 MiB would have held over 12 GB; and Type 0 sampled functions take at most `MAX_SAMPLE_ENTRIES` (2^21) table points and `MAX_SAMPLE_VALUES` (2^23) samples, read no further than `/Size` asks (256 MiB of 1-bit samples asked for over 8 GB); (19) mesh shadings (types 4–7) are sampled only inside the area being drawn (`ShadingPattern::encode_within`, which the vendored hayro renderer calls with that area plus a pixel), within 8 visits per pixel of it plus 4 per triangle (`TriangleSampler`), and patches are triangulated one at a time: points far off the page were sampled over their whole bounding box, up to 65536 × 65536 entries (a fuzzed 147-byte patch stream; a synthetic page passed 6 GB in six seconds), ten thousand overlapping triangles ran for minutes, and every patch became 722 triangles before any limit; meshes hold at most `MAX_MESH_PATCHES` (2^16) patches and `MAX_MESH_TRIANGLES` (2^20) triangles, a lattice needs two to 2^19 vertices per row (`/VerticesPerRow 0` pushed empty rows for ever; one huge row read the whole stream), and a page samples at most `MAX_PAGE_MESH_TRIANGLES` (2^25) mesh triangles in all (a mesh painted a thousand times was triangulated a thousand times); each cut logs a warning; (20) PDF function construction is limited to 64 levels and 10,000 total nodes with cycle detection; calculator parsing and evaluation share procedure depth/work budgets, integer division/bitshift/rotation/index are panic-free, and fixed-size stack errors propagate; (21) a Type 0 font drawn with a substitute that isn't CID-keyed (it isn't embedded, or its program doesn't load) draws `.notdef` for a CID of an Adobe character collection (Japan1, GB1, CNS1, Korea1) that it can't find by Unicode: hayro took the CID for a glyph index of the substitute, which numbers its glyphs its own way, so the character was drawn as an unrelated one (𠮷 as "Ｑ" in BIZ UDPGothic); (22) a Type 0 font drawn with a substitute finds a character given with a variation selector (`/ToUnicode`, or Adobe-Japan1-UCS2, which maps the JIS X 0208 forms of the kanji JIS X 0213:2004 redrew that way: CID 1247 is 噂 U+E0100) through the substitute's variation sequences, else as the character alone: such a CID found no glyph and was drawn as an unrelated one; (23) backport of hayro 0.8's `gradient` module: `EncodedShadingPattern::as_svg_gradient` turns an axial or radial shading into stops of an sRGB gradient (within 0.01 per channel, a stop at every stitching-function bound via `Function::stitching_bounds`) when a native gradient draws it exactly (extended past the box drawn in; a radial one with no background colour); (24) `DecodedImageCache`: decoded image pixels shared across renders through the interpreter cache within a 64 MiB budget (an image-heavy page decoded its thousands of images again per tile and per scale), keyed by every decode input (`DecodedImageKey`: the stream's place and dictionary bytes, its object, mask/stencil/raster output, interpolation, decode target size, preview or final); images under a transfer function and inline images are not cached, an image over the budget is never kept, and a poisoned lock decodes uncached; (25) `Device::actual_text` hands the device a marked content sequence's `/ActualText` (inline or named in `/Properties`), so text extraction keeps the Thai, Indic and Arabic clusters Chrome marks this way (their shaped tone marks and vowels have no Unicode of their own); (26) non-embedded simple fonts drawn with a standard-font stand-in build the Latin Extended-A letters the stand-in lacks (`/Gbreve`, `/Idotaccent`, `/Scedilla`, `/aogonek`, `/ccaron`…) from the base letter and accent it has (`StandardKind::composite_glyph`, `ACCENTED_LETTERS`): PDFium's Foxit stand-ins hold only the Standard/WinAnsi/Mac Roman glyphs, so iText letters with Times New Roman unembedded showed blanks for Ğ, İ, Ş, ğ and ş; the comma-below letters (`/scommaaccent`, `/Tcommaaccent`, `/kcommaaccent`…, found by character, so `/uni0136` and the glyph list's `/Kcedilla` too) are the letter and the font's comma, smaller and under the baseline, since the stand-ins have no `commaaccent` (Romanian ș drew nothing and ț a cedilla in forms laid out from XFA; ģ, whose comma is turned and above, is not built); (27) an embedded TrueType font without a base encoding reads its codes as WinAnsi for text extraction (`EmbeddedKind::code_to_unicode_name`), matching pdftotext's output, instead of Standard: OCR text layers of scans write WinAnsi codes with no `/Encoding`, and Standard has no ü, ö or ß and reads é as Ø (glyph selection unchanged); (28) an image whose pixels hold at most 16 bits of samples (an 8-bit Separation or DeviceN image, a 1-, 2- or 4-bit gray or indexed one) is converted once per possible pixel value through a lookup table instead of once per pixel (`rgb_via_lookup`): a spot-colour tint transform is often a PostScript calculator program, run for every pixel, so a fillable character sheet's 3304 × 4105 DeviceN background took four seconds and 430 MB to draw a page; each entry is converted on its own (`convert_each`), so a tint transform giving the wrong number of components for a value the image never uses cannot shift the colours of the values it does; (29) `Device::begin_annotations`/`end_annotations` bracket the page's annotations, so a device can tell comment paints from document paints (reading colours recolour the document, never a comment, #1548); (30) the Annex D.2 alias codes read as the ink they draw: WinAnsiEncoding 0xA0 and 0xAD, and MacRomanEncoding 0xCA, carry the glyph names `space` and `hyphen` -- the names those tables also give 0x20 and 0x2D -- not `nbspace` and `sfthyphen`, whose glyph list values U+00A0 and U+00AD are invisible formatting characters. Extraction hid drawn ink behind them, so search and redaction matched neither (`XiaoBiaoSong.pdf` in the pdf.js corpus drew 104 soft hyphens; across the 989 files the soft hyphens we extract fall from 117 to 13 and the non-breaking spaces from 30 to 26, what remains coming from `/ToUnicode` maps, which say so explicitly). The base table only, in the text direction only: a `/Differences` name keeps its glyph list value and glyph lookup is untouched, both as pdftotext does; (31) a Type 0 sampled function keeps its samples in one flat array indexed by strides (`Type0::entry`) instead of a hash map keyed by each grid point: the map was built again, one hashed insert per sample, every time a shading using the function was painted (a 2,097,152-sample ramp painted 30 times took 38 s; `bug1721218` in the pdf.js corpus spent most of a 1.5 s page on it); the interpolation is unchanged, so results are bit for bit the same, a sample missing from a short stream still gives no value, and the maximum sample value is computed without overflowing at 32 bits per sample; (32) the decoded-image cache (24) keys a decode by the size the image is drawn at only when a JPX stream decodes it or its soft mask or mask (`decode_reads_target`): JPX is the only filter that decodes a reduced resolution for a size, so a JPEG or Flate scan was decoded again at every zoom step and kept once per zoom level; one decode now serves every size; `InterpreterCache::decoded_image_decodes` counts the cache's decodes; (33) Coons and tensor-product patches copy their vertices' colours less: each point of a patch's 20 × 20 triangle grid is interpolated once (`generate_patch_triangles`; each cell interpolated its four corners itself, 1,444 interpolations a patch for 400 points), a cell's second triangle takes the vertices its first copied, and the mesh sampler moves a patch's triangles into device space instead of copying each vertex (`TriangleSampler::sample_owned`); the same values, 10–16% faster on mesh-gradient pages; (34) `color::tint_transform_runs`: how many colours the calling thread has run through a Separation or DeviceN tint transform (counted once per batch in `convert_f32`), so a test counts patch (28)'s once-per-sample-value runs instead of timing them (its 10 s deadline failed on a busy FreeBSD VM in CI); (35) `EncodedShadingPattern::extent`: where a mesh shading (types 4–7) can paint at all, the pixels its triangles touched when it was encoded (`None` for the types that paint everywhere, and when the shading has a `/Background`), so the renderer samples a texture there alone and skips a mesh with nothing on the canvas; (36) a mesh shading's pixel whose corner no triangle holds strictly (on an edge two triangles share, or on the mesh's side) takes the triangle that covers its centre, edges included (`Triangle::covers`): testing only the corner left a white seam along every shared edge, and the colour is still taken at the corner; (38) the `/DefaultGray`, `/DefaultRGB` and `/DefaultCMYK` colour spaces of a resource dictionary (ISO 32000-2 §8.6.5.6) replace the device space content selects: with `g`/`G`, `rg`/`RG`, `k`/`K` and `cs`/`CS` (by name, or through a `/ColorSpace` resource that is a device space), and as the `/ColorSpace` of an image XObject, an inline image or a shading painted by `sh` or as a shading pattern (`DefaultColorSpaces`, looked up once per content window in the resources and those they inherit, so a form XObject without a default of its own draws in its page's, as Poppler and MuPDF draw it); a default that is a Lab, Indexed, Pattern or device space, has another number of components or is no colour space is ignored and device colour is drawn as before; device spaces inside other spaces (an Indexed base, a Separation or DeviceN alternate, a Pattern's underlying space), shading dictionaries, masks and transparency group spaces are unchanged, and the decoded-image cache (24) keys a decode by the default it was drawn in. hayro drew device colour as it was, so pages that calibrate it this way (common in PDF/A) came out in the wrong colours; (39) knockout groups (#2971): `Device::set_knockout` right after a `/K true` group is pushed; `Device::knockout_image` for an unmasked image before its group is pushed, when `Device::in_knockout_group`: the device clears its placement rectangle only if it will draw the image (on the canvas, not a preview's tiny image, and it decodes), decoded at its draw size so the draw reuses that decode; and, when `Device::knockout_erase_wanted`, a nested group's content drawn once between `begin_knockout_erase` and `end_knockout_erase` before the group itself, which then always gets a layer of its own; (40) an optional content membership dictionary's visibility expression (`/VE`: `/And`, `/Or`, `/Not`, nested up to 32 deep) decides its visibility ahead of `/OCGs` and `/P` (ISO 32000-2 §8.11.2.2); it was ignored, so content under it stayed visible with its layers hidden; a malformed expression, including one naming an object the document doesn't list in `/OCProperties /OCGs`, falls back to `/OCGs` and `/P` (#2986); (41) a transparency group that is neither isolated nor knockout, entered at full opacity with no soft mask and Normal blending, is drawn straight onto the page instead of into a layer of its own (§11.4.7: its elements composite with the backdrop; the layer made a `/BM /Multiply` highlight appearance an opaque block, #1968); (42) text in a Type 3 font is drawn filled whatever the text rendering mode, except mode 3 (invisible): only that mode has any effect on Type 3 fonts (ISO 32000-1 §9.3.6). Stroking ran the glyph procedure a second time, so `2 Tr` made bitmap fonts look bold, `1 Tr` painted an uncoloured glyph in the stroking colour, and `7 Tr` hid it (`7 Tr` since follows 64); (43) Lab colour spaces honour their own `/WhitePoint`: L\*a\*b\* goes to XYZ relative to that white, is Bradford-adapted to D65 and converted to sRGB (ISO 32000-2 §8.6.5.4) instead of through `LAB.icc` as if every white were D50 (a D65 blue came out 45 levels too red; the profile is removed); components normalised to [0, 1] (`manual_scale`, an `/Indexed` palette over Lab) map onto L\* 0..100 and the a\*/b\* `/Range`; (44) a Type 0 font whose `/ToUnicode` is the name `/Identity-H` or `/Identity-V` (not a CMap stream; WSCAD writes it) reads each code as its Unicode value, as Acrobat shows it (`Type0Font::identity_to_unicode`); the identity CMap the name resolved to maps codes to CIDs only, so such pages had no text to select or find; (46) an image XObject's group applies the fill opacity, so the fill alpha is reset to 1 before a stencil mask takes the fill colour as its paint, and a pattern paint drops the opacity it captured at `scn` (`Pattern::without_opacity`) (it was applied twice: a mask at `ca 0.5` was drawn at a quarter, #2975); (47) `path_as_rect`: a five-element path is a rectangle only when its four points are distinct, each step from one to the next runs along a single axis, and the last returns to the first. The length test admits one MoveTo and four LineTo as well as one MoveTo, three LineTo and a ClosePath, and asking only that every corner of the bounding box was visited says nothing about the order or the steps between, so a five-point polyline whose ends reached the corners was painted as that box -- a fourth side the path does not have -- and a clip of that shape was discarded; the coordinates are compared exactly, since the matrix is applied after this check and a `cm` of 10,000 turns `is_nearly_equal`'s 256th of a unit into tens of device units (#3327); (48) an `/ICCBased` colour space is cached by what its profile is read from (`IccProfileKey`): the stream object it names, looked up without reading the stream, and then the stream's dictionary and its own bytes (decrypted, not decoded), so a byte-for-byte copy of a profile in another object is read once, and a profile stream written directly in its array, which reports the object holding the array as every other stream written there does, is told apart by its bytes. hayro keyed it by the stream dictionary's bytes alone, so two different profiles with the same `/N` and `/Length` shared whichever was read first, and colours in the second were drawn through the first. `InterpreterCache::icc_profile_reads` counts the profiles read; (49) `OpenTypeFontBlob::new` also accepts a `post` table version 1.0, 2.0 or 3.0 written with its 16-bit halves swapped (`00 00 00 03`), as ScanSoft PDF Create! embeds every font; such fonts were refused and their text drawn with a substitute (Hebrew came out garbled or missing, #2946); `glyph_names` reads such a table from a copy with the version written correctly, so a 2.0 table's names serve `/Differences`. Any other unknown version is still refused (pdf.js 9462); (50) `CffFontBlob::glyph_index_by_name` looks a glyph name up in a name to glyph map built on first use (shared between clones) instead of searching the whole charset, with a string lookup per glyph, for every character code of a font; the first glyph with a name still wins; (51) at most 4096 graphics states saved at once, holding at most 64 MiB together (each `q` copies the whole state, dash array and clip list included, so short operators multiplied one large state); a `q` past either limit is counted but not copied, and its `Q` still removes the clips added since (from storytold/craft-libs#239); (52) a `/W2` run whose first CID is past `MAX_CID` stops there, as in `/W` (7), checked before the run's metrics are read: a first CID of 4294967295 inserted one entry and then overflowed, discarding the whole `/W2` table (from storytold/craft-libs#254); (55) a Separation or DeviceN tint transform that cannot be read keeps its colour space, and one that cannot be read or evaluated paints the alternate space's initial colour, as evaluation failures already did; that fallback, and a `cs`/`CS` colour space that cannot be read (drawn in DeviceGray as before), are now reported once per content stream as `InterpreterWarning::ColorFallback` (`RenderWarning::ColourFallback` in `pdfcraft-render`) instead of silently (#4260); (56) an annotation whose Invisible flag (bit 1) is set and whose `/Subtype` is none of the standard types of ISO 32000-2 Table 171 (`is_standard_annotation_type`; no `/Subtype` counts as unknown) is not drawn (Table 167), and a `/Popup` annotation's appearance is never painted on the page (§12.5.6.14: a popup has no appearance stream of its own; the viewer shows it as a window for its parent annotation). Both were drawn from their `/AP`; (57) a simple font drawn with a standard-font stand-in because the document names a font it doesn't embed (`StandardKind` with `fallback`) narrows a glyph to a narrower `/Widths` advance but no longer widens it to a wider one: the advance already places the next glyph (ISO 32000-2 §9.2.4; /Widths in Table 109), and widening drew a non-embedded `Arial,Bold` with 600-unit widths as a heavy fixed-pitch face whose `i` and `l` were solid blocks twice their width; an exact standard-14 font still matches its standard metrics both ways; (58) the fallback request for a Type 0 font that is not embedded (`FallbackFontQuery::with_descriptor`) takes its serif, italic and small-cap flags, `/FontWeight`, `/FontFamily` and `/FontStretch` from the descendant CIDFont's font descriptor (ISO 32000-2 §9.7.4.1, §9.7.6.1; §9.8): it read them from the Type 0 dictionary, which has none, so every such request asked for a regular sans-serif face and no resolver could tell a Song or Mincho font from a Hei or Gothic one, or see `/FontWeight 700`; (59) the NoRotate flag (`/F` bit 5) is honoured: the appearance, fitted to `/Rect`, is turned against the page's `/Rotate` about the rectangle's upper-left corner, which stays where it is, so it reads upright as the page is displayed (ISO 32000-2 §12.5.3). Sticky notes, which are saved NoRotate, were drawn turned with the page (#2583). Form fields and links stay in `/Rect`, where PdfCraft takes their click targets from it; (64) text in a Type 3 font follows ISO 32000-2 §9.3.6 in the clipping modes: under `7 Tr` it is not rendered (reported to the device as clipping text, `GlyphDrawMode::Clip`, so extraction keeps it), and in modes 4 to 7 a Type 3 glyph adds nothing to the clipping path (`clip_glyph`), so text shown only in a Type 3 font leaves no clip at `ET`. Since (42) `7 Tr` painted the glyphs in the fill colour (black by default), so a fill meant to follow showed them wherever it didn't cover them; 4 to 6 still render filled; (66) a Separation colour space whose colourant is the special name `All` paints every colourant at once (ISO 32000-2 §8.6.6.4): on screen and in an RGB print raster its tint t is the gray 1 − t, complemented because the device is additive, whatever its alternate space and tint transform say (hayro drew it through the tint transform, so a `/DeviceCMYK` transform giving cyan drew registration marks light cyan); `/None` still paints nothing, any other name still goes through its alternate, and a DeviceN space naming `All` keeps its alternate, since the clause gives the name that meaning in a Separation space; (63) a luminosity soft mask whose group colour space is `/DeviceCMYK` (by name, not an ICC-based or calibrated space) reads a `/DeviceCMYK` fill or stroke colour drawn in it, and its `/BC`, as their gray `1 - min(1, 0.3 c + 0.59 m + 0.11 y + k)` (ISO 32000-2 §10.4.2.3, §11.5.3: device colour converts to gray with no colour calibration; `Context::luminosity_in_device_cmyk`, `color::device_cmyk_to_gray`): it went through the CMYK display profile, where 100% K is a dark grey, so a 100% K mask let about an eighth of the masked paint through. other streams are decoded whole, as before, and share `MAX_DECODED_STREAM`. The content tokenizer reads a window at a time (`UntypedIter::new_window`, `TypedIter::needs_more`, `TypedIter::committed`): an instruction that runs past the window is not decided until more data follows, which `Reader` records by flagging reads and `at_end` past the end of the data, including through the clones the parser makes. The Flate decoder keeps its own 32 KiB history, so it pauses at any output size. `ContentReader::new` reuses raw/decrypted stream bytes for budget accounting and piece creation, and `decoded_raw_within` applies the existing Whole-stream filters and limits to those bytes without decrypting twice; (16) revision 5–6 (AES-256) passwords are tried in their SASLprep form (RFC 4013, then UTF-8, at most 127 bytes, as ISO 32000-2 §7.6.4.3.3 Algorithm 2.A asks and pdfcraft-crypt writes them) and then, if that differs, as given (`aes256_passwords` in `crypto/mod.rs`, which resolves the upstream `TODO: Do the above.`; `stringprep`, already in the tree through pdfcraft-crypt, is an optional dependency enabled by `std`, and without `std` passwords are used as given): the renderer used the password as typed, so one that SASLprep changes (a decomposed `café`, a no-break space, the fullwidth `ａｂ` a Japanese IME types in full-width mode) was wrong, although pdfcraft-cos accepted it: protecting a document with such an open password was rolled back ("the password is incorrect"), and a file with such a password did not open with it.; (17) CCITT `/Rows 0` means the height is not predetermined (ISO 32000-2 Table 11), not zero rows: scanned Group 4 pages written that way rendered blank; (18) The streaming Flate decoder (`lzw_flate::flate::fallback`) copies a back-reference in runs of up to its distance (`extend_from_within`), not byte by byte. The copy reads only bytes already in the output, and a copy whose source does not exist still writes nothing, so the bytes are those a byte-by-byte copy writes. Inflating the A1 sample's content stream (278.6 MB) takes about 14% less time (0.66 s to 0.56 s); the output is identical; (19) CCITT `/Rows` below the image's `/Height` decodes to the height: a plotter driver wrote `/Rows` equal to `/Columns`, so only the first rows were decoded and the rest drawn black (#3308) (20) `stream` followed by spaces or tabs and then the line break (`stream \r\n`, as Microsoft Reporting Services writes it) starts the data after the line break; the content stream was taken to start at the space and the page rendered blank.; (21) a JP2 colour specification naming an enumerated colour space the decoder refuses (CIEJab in a veraPDF fixture, YCbCr, PhotoYCC, YPbPr, bilevel…) no longer fails the image: it is decoded again from a copy whose `colr` names the space the decoder assumes without one, greyscale, sRGB or CMYK by component count, as MuPDF and Poppler draw it (`without_refused_enumerated_colour`; the page drew blank, #3306); (22) an object stream's index of `objnum offset` pairs is parsed once per stream and kept beside its decoded data (`ObjectStreamIndexes`, `XRef::with_object_stream_indexes`), and an offset past `usize` is malformed instead of wrapping: `XRef::get_with` parsed the whole index again for every object it fetched from the stream, so reading all of a stream of N objects took N² steps (a Firefox page whose 65,542 objects share one stream took 37 s to draw and 40 s to extract its text); (23) the inline-image end-of-data look-ahead no longer rejects a candidate `EI` because a byte above 0x7F lies between it and the next one: when the candidate is the end, those bytes are the content stream that follows the image, and its strings carry such bytes (WinAnsi `(Grüße) Tj`, the two-byte codes of any Type 0 font), so the operator check that follows decides alone, bounded as in (4) (a scanned page whose OCR text held an accented word and a later capital "EI" — EINGANG, BEI, KLEIN — drew and extracted nothing after the image: 40 of 275 pages across five real documents); (24) `xref::prev_offset`: a trailer `/Prev` written as a reference `N G R` is read as the offset that object holds when the section's own entries place it (iText's `indirectPrev.pdf`; each section's entries are read before its `Prev` is followed), and otherwise as offset N (tiff2pdf; JHOVE's PDF-HUL-157 files, #2366), as `pdfcraft-cos` and other readers take it, so the earlier sections' pages are seen instead of one; (25) direct arrays and dictionaries share a reader-local nesting cap of 128, counted while skipping and while parsing a dictionary (its lenient repair reads, rather than skips, an object found where a key belongs, so `<< << …` recursed through that read); deeper objects return `None` instead of overflowing the stack (including unused trailer values, trailer entries, content operands and marked-content properties); a chain of 65 direct stitching functions now stops at this cap, before the 64-function guard; (26) an xref stream subsection must be backed by its decoded data: all-zero `/W` widths (an entry reads no bytes) and a declared count longer than the data are refused before any entry is inserted, where a tiny stream with a large `/Size` or `/Index` count inserted that many entries (from storytold/craft-libs#239); a subsection running past object number `i32::MAX` is refused instead of overflowing or turning negative; (27) an xref stream's type field is read big-endian at its full `/W[0]` width, where only its first byte was read and wider fields shifted every later entry, and `/W[0]` over 8 bytes is refused like `/W[1]` (from storytold/craft-libs#241); (28) a content instruction keeps up to 256 operands (`MAX_OPERANDS`) instead of 10, and past that drops the oldest instead of ending the content stream: the eleventh operand of a twelve-ink DeviceN `scn` (ISO 32000-2 §8.6.6.5 allows any number of components) blanked the rest of the page (#4260) | (1) `cos/tests/writer.rs::page_tree_loops_in_object_streams_do_not_crash_readers`; Same goal as [winit#4478](https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit/pull/4478), whose changes don't reach this call order (macOS 14); to be proposed upstream there; (10) on macOS, when the first key in a fresh app reaches Apple Korean's `insertText` as a raw compatibility jamo instead of starting a composition, that key is interpreted once more, synchronously, before it is sent as `KeyboardInput` (g k s typed ㅎㅏㄴ instead of 한); only an unmodified, non-repeated first key whose one callback inserts that same jamo, with IME enabled and nothing composed, focus and input source unchanged, is retried (`ime_startup.rs`). `hayro-postscript` is the crates.io 0.1.0 package plus patch (1). The local Cargo
registry cache metadata for that package (`.cargo_vcs_info.json`) records upstream
VCS commit `a2354aebaf86f5ab13e5fd6b6b0521306488bf9d`. The registry copy and this vendored tree's
source files differ only in `src/object.rs` (the patch above); the vendored tree
omits the registry dotfiles `.cargo_vcs_info.json` and `.cargo-ok`, so the upstream
commit is recorded here.

Renderer startup errors: `egui-wgpu::RenderState::create` also wraps `Renderer::new` in
`winit::catch_errors` when the winit feature is enabled. A rejected shader or render pipeline
is returned as `WgpuError::CreateRenderer`, allowing PdfCraft's existing startup OpenGL retry.
The regression `pdfcraft` `tests::pipeline_creation_error_is_returned_and_device_remains_usable`
uses an invalid three-sample pipeline, then valid and invalid pipelines again on the same device.
Later rendering errors, device loss, and non-winit renderer construction are unchanged.

Stencil masks filled with a pattern (#2975): `hayro`'s renderer paints a pattern-filled stencil mask with the fill (non-stroking) paint. It passed `is_stroke = true`, so an uncoloured tiling pattern was drawn in its stroke colour (black by default) instead of the colour given with `scn`. Covered by `raster::tests::stencil_masks_are_drawn_at_the_fill_opacity_once` (the uncoloured tiling pattern case).

Temporary: hayro is the bootstrap renderer and lopdf the bootstrap inspector (ADR-0004); M2.6 replaces them with our own devices and `cos`/`model`.

TIFF predictor decoding: hayro-syntax aligns the output writer to a byte boundary after each
row before splitting off its buffer. Packed RGB samples at 1, 2 or 4 bits per component can
leave padding bits; without alignment later rows overwrite the preceding row or decode empty.
Covered by `raster::tests::tiff_predictor_packed_rgb_rows_keep_their_byte_boundaries` (including
horizontal differencing and an 8-bit control) and
`raster::tests::tiff_predictor_packed_rgb_image_renders_every_row`.

JPEG 2000 palettes (#3179): `hayro-syntax::filter::jpx::decode` applies a JP2 palette (`pclr`)
when the image dictionary has no `/ColorSpace`, since the colour then comes from the JP2 header
(ISO 32000-2 §7.4.9). With a `/ColorSpace` the raw indices are kept, as an `/Indexed` space needs.
A `/ColorSpace` that does not resolve counts as none: the JP2 colours are then the only ones.
Without the patch a palette image with no `/ColorSpace` was drawn as its indices, in gray.
The resolved colours are 8-bit samples whatever the precision of the indices (a 1-bit index no
longer rescales its colours to 0 or 255 per channel); an image without a palette keeps its own.
Covered by `filter::jpx::tests::jpx_palette_is_applied_without_a_color_space`,
`filter::jpx::tests::jpx_palette_indices_stay_raw_for_an_indexed_color_space`,
`filter::jpx::tests::palette_colours_are_eight_bit_and_other_samples_keep_their_precision` and
`raster::tests::a_jp2_palette_keeps_its_colours_whatever_the_index_precision`.

Glyph names outside the Adobe Glyph List (#3169, #3170): hayro-interpret's `glyph_name_to_text`
maps a name by the glyph list specification's full mapping (drop from the first `.`, split on `_`,
each part through the list, `uniXXXX…` or `uXXXX`; a `uni` part with any group that isn't a
character maps to nothing), so `f_i`, `f_l` and `hyphen.case` read as text. A name that only
numbers the glyph (`C39`, `c251`) still reads as nothing: the code's StandardEncoding character
would be a guess, wrong wherever the font's /Encoding puts the glyph elsewhere (review on #3239). Covered by `text::tests::glyph_names_outside_the_glyph_list_still_read_as_text`.

Text extraction: hayro-interpret exposes `OutlineGlyph::is_vertical` from a Type0 font’s CMap writing mode. PdfCraft follows negative glyph-space y for WMode 1 so upright vertical columns can be searched (#126).

Lab Bradford follow-up to #1237: Lab adapts XYZ to D65 with white-point ratios
computed in Bradford LMS coordinates. CalRGB's existing flat-white and
black-point normalization is unchanged. `lab_bradford_tests` checks independent
D50/equal-energy neutral and chromatic oracles, D65 identity, and direct/Indexed
consistency (including an asymmetric chromatic Range), and zero/overflowing
cone-response fallback.

## Clipping-only text reporting (#3109 / #3116)

`hayro-interpret/src/interpret/text.rs` reports mode 7 glyphs after installing their
clip, and `hayro-interpret/src/types.rs` distinguishes `GlyphDrawMode::Clip` from
invisible OCR text. `hayro/src/renderer.rs` does not paint either mode directly.
This preserves clipping-only titles when `TextFilter.images` excludes invisible OCR.
Coverage: `text::tests::clipping_mode_filter_keeps_titles_and_excludes_ocr` (plain
and ActualText filtered extraction), and
`text::tests::clipping_mode_text_is_extracted_and_searchable_like_other_rendering_modes`
(extraction, search, glyph geometry, clip-through pixels and no-paint pixels).

Missing spacing glyphs (#3601): in `hayro-interpret` `Type0Font::map_via_unicode`,
an OpenType substitute uses its ordinary-space glyph only when its own charmap
lacks a spacing character (including Adobe-Japan1 U+2002). Native glyphs and
variation forms retain priority; embedded fonts, PDF advances and Unicode decoding
are unchanged. Renderer regressions `japanese_substitute_missing_spaces_draw_no_ink`
and `japanese_substitute_spaces_keep_pdf_widths_and_unicode` use the synthetic
MS-Mincho / UniJIS-UCS2-HW-H fixture with craft-fonts, including `/W` and `/DW`
placement controls.

Symbolic TrueType `cmap` order (#4156): in `hayro-interpret` `EmbeddedKind::map_code`, an
embedded TrueType font whose Nonsymbolic flag is not set (the branch `is_non_symbolic()` does not
take) looks a code up in its Windows (3, 0) or (3, 1) subtables before its Macintosh and Unicode
ones, as ISO 32000-2 §9.6.5.4 prescribes for symbolic fonts; the
(1, 0) subtable still serves codes the (3, x) ones leave out. The records were tried in the
order the font lists them, platform ID first, so a wrong (1, 0) table (SAS 9.4's AMT fonts)
drew "8" as "p" and "+" as "V". Covered by `raster::tests::symbolic_truetype_cmap`, whose font
is built in memory.
